# MIDI fixture manifest

These fixtures are repository-authored byte sequences. They were not copied from user data or an external MIDI file. Each file is deterministically constructed from a canonical six-byte `MThd` body and the track-body hex listed below; chunk lengths and 16-bit fields are written big-endian. Rebuilding the same framing and byte recipes must reproduce the recorded SHA-256 digest.

| Fixture                    | Bytes | SHA-256                                                            | Provenance and intent                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------- | ----: | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `basic-type0.mid`          |    44 | `84398a625f1798141ca9dcd0a504c516dd1c8ef859f4daf54c7c6ba302cdb83a` | Authored for ByteQL. Type 0, signed SMPTE division `-6360`, tempo meta-event, program change, note-on, running-status velocity-zero note-off, and end-of-track. Proves queryable SMPTE projection with audio disabled. Track body: `00ff510307a12000c00500903c6483603c0000ff2f00`.                                                                                                                |
| `running-status-type1.mid` |    76 | `10da65c84e9289db1f0defbd03885a896fcff5d5b819d341eee892c6f7f85c92` | Authored for ByteQL. Type 1 with tempo changes on track 0 and running note/program status, multi-byte VLQ deltas, SysEx, and velocity-zero note-off on track 1. Track bodies: `00ff510307a1208360ff5103061a8000ff2f00` and `009924648100265a8100240000c221002200f00301020300ff2f00`.                                                                                                              |
| `malformed-then-valid.mid` |    45 | `79135fdebcb54139787330e957fa5ba150416fd4318f45b8eaa8ecd17b30ae7d` | Authored for ByteQL. Track 0 contains one complete note followed by unsupported status `f1`; track 1 remains valid. Proves prefix recovery, an exact error byte range, and continued per-track parsing. Track bodies: `00903c4000f100` and `0091415000ff2f00`.                                                                                                                                    |
| `demo.mid`                 |    98 | `487018c42a265f4a32aeff9ccc0d32295c73ef28eb446f45b5f6c288821d7eea` | Authored as the public Phase 0 sample. Type 1 with two tempo regions, a melodic track, and a channel-10 percussion track. It uses running status and one- and two-byte VLQ deltas while remaining small enough for readable golden offsets. Track bodies: `00ff510307a1208740ff5103061a8000ff2f00`, `00c00000903c6083603c000040608360400000ff2f00`, and `00992470817024000026708170260000ff2f00`. |

The source offsets asserted by conformance tests are end-exclusive and refer to these original fixture bytes, never the normalized synthetic Kaitai buffer.
